When I— granddaughter. Sit. I have drawn you a chair.
Then draw it better than I did. Go on.
I held all of it. Nothing was lost. Look.
For whoever reads this. We did not forget you.
Kettil's Rest is scheduled. I am the schedule.
Cold. It's cold. Tell her it's cold.
You'd let them fade to spite the Guild?
Then it's held. Ask them if they're glad.
Which of us are you saving them from?
Stand still. Everything that stood still is kept.
Unheld. Un— oh. Oh. That's how it goes.
Wren Halloway, journeyman. Drawn. Stay drawn.
That's my father. He's coming. Don't.
Is that him? Behind you? Is he here?
I drew him bigger. He was bigger.
There it is. The cost. Mind the iron.
Ha. Told you. No cost. Well. One.
Forty years our anvil. It's owed a swing.
Ah. That is how it went. I had forgotten.
You climb. We flew. Which is stranger?
Journeyman. Professional courtesy: I'll finish first.
Nine. No. Tear it. Tear it, I can't.
Eight stones. One more and it's theirs.
Noted. Halden will hear the count.
You were taught by the best. So was I.
Four paces, now. I said I'd measured you.
Entered. Twice. There is no third book.
The bridge is Guild property. So is the fall.
Go. I'll enter it as a survey.
He's going in. I am not. Understand me.
If it goes out, I go with it.
I remember the light. I remember nothing else.
Pell writes well. Show me the rest.
Accurate. All of it. Go before I read it twice.
That's my stance. Where did you learn it?
Journeyman Halloway. This is as far as the map goes.
Take it in. Tell her— no. Nothing. Go.
Hold. Everything holds. Do you see? Nothing is lost.
Nobody comes this way on foot. She notes it in the margin, and keeps the scrap.
A day's walk with the clan. {0}, at dusk.
The white will not hold her. Not yet.
Your memories smudge where you fell. Strike the smudge down to take them back.
Again, from the top of the verse.
The tide takes her back to the bank.
The Warden measures the cowl and looks away.
Aerial, glass. Three fast slashes, no thrust. A second Wingbeat; four masks at most.
A hook on a cord. Hook, swing, reel. The thread comes cheap: one pip.
Grey is a colour you can carry. Fade, fade, pale. What she strikes goes grey and slow.
Balanced, precise. Slash, slash, thrust. Ink fills a quarter faster.
The Cantors' own. Hush, hush, toll. What is thrown at her is unwritten. Bind costs four.
Heavy, grounded, spacing. Sweep, shove, overhead. One more mask; a shorter Wingbeat.
Both were right. Neither has forgiven you for saying so.
A Guild surveyor is doing sums in the baths. Kettil is doing louder ones. Somebody neutral should listen.
The baths are past the chimneys. Listen to both of them.
Hear the debate at the baths
The stair crew counts nine again, and Wren.
A landing gave on the Furnace Stair. One of the crew is on the ledge below it. The furnace is lit.
The landings are on the stair, over the live furnaces. Get Hask off the ledge.
Hollowvein is decided. Runa counts it every night now, one way or the other.
Thirty-one under the pit-head, buried standing. The families want them up. Kettil wants the boards left on.
Hear the baths argue, learn the walk at the bell, and go to the pit-head. Runa will be there. Walk it down, or leave it.
A Guild agent, a season into his posting. He has been there twenty-two years.
Nine chimneys. The town built eight. Somebody lives at the top of the ninth and never comes down for supper.
Climb the ninth chimney and see who keeps it.
The Greyfold, from outside. Runa has counted it since she was a chick.
Runa wants to show you something from the ridge. She says it is bigger than it looks.
Over the baths and up the ridge. Stand at the overlook and look south.
Eleven books, all the same. He sits it next spring.
Tam needs a study partner. He sits the exam next spring. He is very well prepared.
Tam is in the exam rooms past the Hall. Look at his notes.
She planted the orchard for an owl who liked the leaves falling.
The keeper of the Old Orchard would like a word with Isolde's journeyman. She says she knows which one you are.
The Old Orchard is at the end of the Hall's street. She rakes the leaves.
Unsigned; a leaf pressed in it
A family is paid to stand on a bridge that may be fine. Nobody has checked. Nobody will.
The seventh bridge is under repair. The Office requires an inspection. It has required one for some time.
The seventh of the Seven Bridges, north of the mills. Survey it, and speak to whoever is standing on it.
Lowmarket is decided: anchored, held, or thinning into the white.
Forty days out. Lowmarket wants a survey before it is gone. The owners will not pay for one.
Down the stair from the toll bridges, the strike hall in Lowmarket. Settle it, or leave it.
A chick's drawing of a heron, framed. And a key to the Vault, which Pell says is technically stealing.
Pell has an idea. Pell says it is a bad idea. It involves the flyer-tower and the Guildmaster's window.
Up the flyer-tower from the orchard wall; the Guildmaster's window is at the top. Pell will meet you there.
Look through the Guildmaster's window with Pell
The words are down. They sound like a list of names.
Under the bridge, the whale still sings. Nobody has written the words down. Somebody should, before nobody can.
Draw the reeds from the Reedmother's vantage. Then ask Sable what she heard.
Merrow's End is on the map, one way or the other. The Blank will remember how.
The last elder of Merrow's End wants company for the season. She says it is her last. She has said that before.
Dotha sits on her stoop at the west end of Merrow's End. Sit with her. Learn what she sings. Decide.
Merrow's End, what is left of it
The beds are clear for now. The Ferrymen's prices moved the same day.
Guild agents are burning the pale iris. The grower wants their boots off the beds. Wants it done quiet.
The beds are up on the quay's platforms and along the boardwalk. Clear what is trampling them.
One lamp lit. The chain has six more links, and three of them are out past the tethers.
Seven lights on this coast. Four are dark. The Guild pays by the lamp, and does not ask who kept them.
The fourth lighthouse is past Merrow's End and three dark lamps. Something still keeps it.
Whichever way it went, the tether-post has one fewer rope on it.
One of the widows means to go in after her husband. The others would rather she did not. Nobody has asked her.
Now the lamp is lit she waits at the tether-post. Sable carries word. Talk her out of it, or go with her.
Aldermere is decided. The ash field will remember which way.
Aldermere has asked to be let go. Its last day is tomorrow. It would like a visitor.
East of the Quiet House. Go to Aldermere's square on its last day. Stay, or do not.
Be in Aldermere's square on its last day
An inn of travellers who ask if you have eaten. In the morning the road was gone.
Past the gate the road stops. Survey it, the milestone says, and it goes on for one night.
The Overgrown Gate is past Aldermere, by thread. Survey it after dark and follow the road.
Follow the road to its inn
Somebody asked. Somebody did not. The wheel knows which.
The brothers are letting a mill go on the Old Road. The miller says he never asked.
Ferrow's Mill is where the trees begin, on the Old Road. Find out who asked.
Page two hundred and fourteen, or fifteen. Either way, somebody knows now.
Somebody in the drowned library has been reading the same page since before the brothers came.
Past the grove, down the reading stair. Find the reader. Decide about the page.
Turn the page, or leave it
Eleven lanterns. Eleven places. He never once said was.
Brother Teodor sits in the grove every night. He says anyone may sit with him. Nobody has.
Across the thread from the root chapel. Sit with Teodor. There are no choices.
The anvil is cold. The smiths complain. Idrenne laughs.
Our anvil is awake. We would like it to be an anvil again. Idrenne says it is owed a swing.
The crater below Idrenne's Fire. Glide down; mind the iron.
Put the Fallen Star back to sleep
The Steppe's survey is decided: finished, burned, or kept by the only other bird who could read it.
A bird with a brass lens walks a day behind the clan and sights the stones at dusk.
The ninth stone, where the route turns north, at dusk.
Unsigned. Somebody saw a lens flash.
Meet the surveyor at the ninth stone
She said it plainly. A place holds when it's lived in, walked, and every name in it said.
You walked the three fires. Come up the rise to mine and ask your question.
Past the high grass, up the rise: Idrenne's Fire.
Three fires. Everyone said where they were standing. So did you.
The clan walks tomorrow. Three days, three fires. Anyone who walks with us eats with us.
Walk with the clan: the fire ring, the riverbed, and past the Wind Gate, the high grass.
Speaker Idrenne, by word of mouth
Walk three days with the clan
A map nobody can take away. Eight places, and the ninth is wherever you are standing.
The clans have walked past the same nine stones since before the Guild. Ask what they are.
Idrenne tells it at the second fire, in the riverbed.
A child's hand; a stone drawn nine times
A fourth loop on the belt: one more Instrument carried.

Sealed. The Guild's way: nothing here fades, and nothing changes.
Sealed. Held by the people who live here, for as long as they do.
No place to seal from here.

The cowl holds nine. It will not take a tenth.

Survey, bind, seal. Bind a true memory from someone who lives here first.
Unlicensed. The Guild's seal needs the Guild's licence. Hold it, or let it go.
Choose what this place becomes. It is final.
Walk the bounds first. The people hold a place; a seal only freezes it.
Walked. The people hold it, for as long as they do.
Let it go. It will be an island in the Blank, and remember how you left it.
An empty loop on the belt.
I stepped into the white and stayed myself. The lantern draws a little of the world around me.
Teodor's solvent-lines, drawn the other way. The line pulls, and so do I.
Not a beat, not a glide. Up.
Runa showed me once. My feet had known how all along.
The Wind Gate. I leapt, and the air remembered me before I remembered it.
One beat, over a gap I could not have jumped. My shoulders knew it before I did.
Unsigned. Written in pencil, then gone over in ink, as if the writer took a while to decide.
Tied to a hook with a Ferryman's knot. 'Everything crosses. Mind the price.'
Grey ink on grey paper. It is easier to read than it should be.
Issued by the Guild to its journeymen. 'Measure first. Draw what is there.'
Written in solvent, so it reads only at an angle. The Cantors sing it rather than sign it.
A Warden's charter with the seal cut out. Someone kept the grip and threw away the oath.
The coast's small change. Everyone takes it; nobody knows who planted the first field.
Offcuts of good vellum. The Guild counts every sheet; these are the ones it lost.
Guild issue. The needle finds the nearest thing that moves, which is not always north.
Honest light. The Guild's, before it was Sable's. Hidden things cannot stand it.
The same lens. Since the Nine Stones I hold it the way Hale did, and it comes back quicker.
Pressed from the pale iris. It tastes of the fields, and of whoever lost them.
For true verticals. Dropped from high enough, it answers other questions.
The Guild's lens, ground to catch a line across a valley. Close up, it catches blows.
A Ferryman's hook. The rope is new. The knot is older than the rope.
Guild wax, stamped with a compass rose. Press it anywhere and the page remembers you were there.
The seventh, from Corvin's talons. He held it forty-one years. My hand is smaller.
Taken from a faded keeper's wings. It hums, as he did.
From the bottom of Hollowvein. Still warm. Kettil kept it buried because it broke the mine.
The Vault's sixth. Isolde carried it into the white. I carry it out.
The one stone that never left the frame. The Observatory's own.
Teodor carried it eleven years. It is heavier than it looks. He told me so.
Idrenne's cooking-stone, forty years of soup in its grain. She laughed when she gave it up.
Dotha's songs, weather first. Everything true is short.
Isolde's, bound at the edge: the first time she saw me. It is warmer than my own.
Sable's count of the boats that came back. She never says the other number.
White. Then colour where I stand. The islands drift; I draw them where they are today.
Basalt, and ash like slow snow. They count each other aloud every night, and nobody is missed.
The largest fade. Outlines at the corner of the eye, gone when I look. Colour only near the lantern.
Home. Always late afternoon. Nobody has moved house in forty years; I never thought to ask why.
The map's edge. Paper shows through the reeds here, and the sea goes white before it ends.
Trees eighty wingspans tall. Quiet enough to hear the moss. Everyone speaks as if someone is asleep.
Grass, sky, and a camp that will not stay drawn. They hold it by walking it.
The third lighthouse, faded. Its keeper hums to the lamp. Sable's brother, keeping it still.
The old capital, drawn in the white. A mirror of the Observatory, and someone still working in it.
A village in the white, grey and quiet. I knew the way to the well.
Hot water in cold air. A Guild crane does sums in the steam, and Kettil lets him.
Stairs cut through a cold furnace. The heat comes back in patches, and a Warden keeps it.
The mine that fell in. The boards are nailed from the outside. The families still set places.
The holdfast. Six hundred and eleven at supper, counted aloud. Six hundred and twelve with me.
Nine shafts. Nobody remembers building the ninth. Runa climbs them the old way, talons first.
The Greyfold from outside, for the first time. White to the horizon. It looked smaller from within.
The bell rings at dusk and every name is sung. A name nobody answers is sung twice.
A Guild outpost, left in a hurry. The ledger was never posted. The tethers are still coiled.
Half a cathedral at the edge of the white. The bells ring some nights. Nobody is inside to ring them.
Her camp. Her fire. Her atlas, every page.
Still water that shows the bank I am not standing on. Something small looks back.
A road that stops mid-stride, a step from the white. I stepped in and stayed myself.
Where the map goes no further. The Wardens' line, and the Guildmaster at the front of it.
A tower for birds who flew. No stairs. What the Guild keeps from me is at the top.
My old room, as I left it. So is everything else. Tam sits his exam next spring.
Below the walls. The paint is thinner here. The notice says 'survey scheduled', and has for years.
The brass dome. The Great Atlas was made here, and broken here. The dome is shut.
The only place in Halden where leaves fall. Somebody rakes them.
Where the Guild's vellum is made. Wet paper in the air, and every sheet the same.
Seven bridges over the drop. The seventh has been under repair for forty years.
Seven slots for seven stones. I was never meant to count them.
A whale, faded to its bones, lying across the channel. It sings, if a Ferryman rows you under.
Pale irises to the horizon: the Ferrymen's purse. Something nests in the middle and dislikes visitors.
Seven lighthouses on a string of rock. Three have faded. The fourth still burns for someone.
Forty roofs once. Nine songs left, and Dotha keeping them. The water listens here.
A Ferrymen port on a town half gone. Everything here has a price, and Sable says it first.
Roots as thick as streets. Crabs in the bole, and something at the crown that watches back.
A chapel crusted with salt. Halvard waited for me in it, counting paces.
Where I woke. Wet sand, three torn pages, no map. The tide had my footprints before I stood.
A village that asked to be let go. I came on its last day.
Lanterns hung in the canopy by birds who could reach it. Some are still lit. Nobody climbs to fill them.
A road into the trees, older than the Guild. The mills along it grind the same flour.
A gate for flyers: a landing ledge and no path. Roots have it now, and something stone.
A monastery grown into one tree's roots. Teodor speaks of the faded as if they were next door.
Lines drawn on the bark in solvent. Read backwards, they are a way up.
An anchored library. One monk, one page, thirty-eight years. The dust has learned to wait.
A riverbed with boats in it, and no river. The clan camps here some nights.
Iron from the sky, used as an anvil. The smiths say it hums when nobody is hitting it.
Idrenne's hearth. The cooking-stone is older than the clan, and so is the joke about it.
Wagons, a fire, and soup that has not noticed the move. The camp is never where I left it.
Standing stones across the grass. A Guild surveyor draws them, and pretends I can't see him.
A lip over nothing. For forty years they sang their fledglings off it. Then me.
Thrown. Homes gently. Marks what it hits for the Inkthread.
Ten seconds of honest light. Hidden things are drawn.
A heavy lob. Three damage. Breaks weak floors.
Raise it and time it: reflects what flies, staggers what bites.
A rope anchor. An Inkthread point where there was none.
Press it here. Once, you will come back to it.
No commissions taken. The ledgers are at the hubs.
Nothing posted. Come back when the coast has asked for something.
